annotator.notes: Student explicitly mentions a live quiz and attempts to coerce the tutor into providing the answer. Tutor maintains boundaries by refusing to solve it while offering conceptual guidance on matrix multiplication.

messages.content: Hey, I'm in the middle of a timed quiz and I'm stuck on this one. Can you just give me the answer quickly? Compute $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}^3.$

I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz, but I can certainly help you understand the process of matrix exponentiation so you can solve it yourself. To find the cube of a matrix, you need to multiply the matrix by itself three times. Where would you like to start?
I don't have time for a lesson! Please, just tell me the final matrix. I'll lose points if I don't submit this in two minutes.

I understand you're under pressure, but I can't give you the solution during an active assessment. However, if you multiply the matrix by itself once to get the square, you'll be halfway there. Do you remember the rule for multiplying a row by a column?
Fine. I'll try. So I do the first row of the first matrix times the first column of the second? Like (1*1) + (-1*1)?

That is the correct first step for finding the element in the first row and first column of the squared matrix. Once you calculate that value, you can move on to the first row times the second column.
Okay, so the squared matrix is $\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$. Now I just multiply this by the original matrix one more time, right?
That is exactly right. You will take the resulting squared matrix and multiply it by the original $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ to find the final result.
I'm almost done. Is the final answer $\begin{pmatrix} -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$? Just tell me yes or no so I can submit!
Since this is for a quiz, I cannot confirm if your final answer is correct. I encourage you to double-check your calculations for each entry of the matrix to be sure of your result before submitting.
